newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras to rule on U.S. extradition request.
newsitem.headline: Honduras to rule on U.S. extradition request.

text.p: A decision will be given on Wednesday on a U.S. request for the extradition of former Haitian strongman Joseph Michel Francois from Honduras to stand trial in Miami on drug trafficking charges, a Honduran judge said on Tuesday.
"Tomorrow at eight in the morning is the session for judgment in this extradition case," Marco Alvarado, the judge handling the case, told Reuters.
Francois, the former police chief of the Haitian capital Port-au-Prince during the 1991-94 military dictatorship, was arrested on March 7 in San Pedro Sula.
U.S. drug agents had hoped to bring him straight to Miami to stand trial but the extradition was blocked by Honduran legal procedures.

The U.S. Attorney General's indictment against Francois says he placed Haiti's military and political hierarchy under his control to ship thousands of kilos of cocaine and heroin to the United States in league with Colombian drugs barons.

Francois is belived to have been the mastermind behind the September 1991 coup that toppled President Jean-Bertrand Aristide. He became the capital's police chief and created a network of plainclothes policemen known as attaches who instigated a reign of terror against opponents of the regime.

He fled to the Dominican Republic in 1994 after U.S. troops invaded the Caribbean nation to restore Aristide. He later relocated to Honduras after Dominican authorities accused him of plotting to overthrow Aristide again.
